title: Sidecar <-> Godot protocol, version 1
description: Every WebSocket message is one JSON object matching exactly one entry below. Event types (sidecar -> Godot) are past tense; command types (Godot -> sidecar) are imperative. See NOTES.md -> Protocol.

provider_id.description: Provider key, e.g. "claude". Also the extension namespace.

seq.description: Per-session event counter, starting at 1. A snapshot carries the current value; later events for that session continue from it. A gap means Godot missed an event and should send session.get_snapshot.

state.description: working: both roles. waiting: both roles, needs the user (see reason). idle: orchestrator only, turn finished. done: subagent only, result returned; may be resumed (back to working). error: both roles.

state_reason.description: Why an agent is waiting or errored, e.g. "permission", "question" or "input" when waiting. Null otherwise.

path.description: Absolute path of the working directory.

name.description: Display name; defaults to the folder name.

repo.description: Set by the sidecar on sessions: the git repository's main folder, the same for all its worktrees. Absent outside git. Ignored in commands.

parent.description: The agent that spawned this one; null for the orchestrator. Agents form a tree.

task.description: Short description of what it was asked to do.

label.description: What choosing it does, in the provider's words; shown as is.

summary.description: One human-readable line, e.g. "Run: npm install".

input.description: Raw tool input, for a details view.

options.description: Other ways to allow, beyond a plain allow, in the order the provider's own interface lists them (e.g. Claude Code's "Yes, and don't ask again for: npm test *", "Yes, and switch to auto mode"). permission.respond's option is one of these.

asked_at.description: Set by the sidecar: when it first saw the request. Ignored from providers.

mode.description: A permission mode (permission_modes capability): the provider's own id, e.g. Claude Code's "default", "acceptEdits", "plan" or "auto". Godot shows its own name for ids it knows, else the id.

plan.description: A plan an agent asks the user to approve before it acts on it (plans capability).

text.description: The plan, Markdown. It is also in the chat as a message of kind plan.

modes.description: The modes approving can switch to, in the order the provider's own interface offers them. plan.answer's mode is one of these.

asked_at.description: Set by the sidecar: when it first saw the plan. Ignored from providers.

question.description: Clarifying questions an agent asks the user, as one set (questions capability).

asked_at.description: Set by the sidecar: when it first saw the questions. Ignored from providers.

usage_limit.description: One of the account's usage limits (usage capability): how much of it is used, and when it starts over. id: a stable name per provider (Claude: five_hour, seven_day). label: the provider's own words for it (Claude: "5-hour", "Weekly"), shown as plain text (untrusted).

label.description: No control characters (no new lines) and no bidi overrides, so it can't fake a line or another provider's text.

used_percent.description: 0 to 100 (may pass 100 once over the limit).

usage.description: How many tokens a session uses (usage capability), the whole current figures. tokens: the conversation's totals so far, each API call counted once. context: how full the context window is after the latest call (input, cache reads and cache writes); null until the first call. turn: the turn going on or last finished: the user message that started it (null before the first) and the output tokens of its calls so far. limits: the account's usage limits, a list (empty while none are known).

percent.description: How full, 0 to 100; null when the provider doesn't say.

window.description: The context window's size in tokens; null when the provider doesn't say.

limits.description: In the provider's order, each id once; empty while none are known.

session.description: Full state of one session (one island).

native_id.description: The provider's own session ID (e.g. Claude's session UUID). Null until the provider assigns one, or if it has none.

origin.description: app: started from this app. external: attached to a session running elsewhere (not in v1).

capabilities.description: Capabilities the provider declares for this session, keyed by capability name, each with its own config object. Capability events are only sent when declared.

extensions.description: Extension namespaces this session may send, e.g. ["claude"].

agents.description: Every agent, orchestrator first. Includes done subagents.

questions.description: Pending questions. Present only when the questions capability is declared.

mode.description: The current permission mode; null until the provider knows it. Present only when the permission_modes capability is declared.

plans.description: Plans waiting for approval. Present only when the plans capability is declared.

usage.description: Token usage, null until the first count. Present only when the usage capability is declared.

notices.description: Current notices, at most one per code.

notice.description: Something the user should know about a session that isn't an agent's state, e.g. a setting that limits what the world can show.

code.description: Machine-readable; Godot shows its own text for codes it knows. confirm_in_terminal: the provider needs the user in its own window to start the session (create/resume replies only). transcripts_off: the provider isn't saving transcripts, so some features may not work as intended. hooks_unavailable: the provider's session isn't reporting its activity (chat still works). conversation_cleared: a new conversation started in the session (it remembers nothing of the chat before). conversation_resumed: the session switched to an earlier conversation; its chat (session.get_history) is now that conversation's. conversation_moved: the conversation went on somewhere the world can't reach; continue it in the provider's own window.

message.description: English fallback text for codes Godot doesn't know.

message_kind.description: What a message is, when it isn't plain chat. plan: a plan the agent presents for approval (plans capability), shown full width.

turn_tokens.description: A user message only (usage capability): the output tokens of the turn it started.

summary.description: One human-readable line, as in tool.started.

result.description: One line about how it ended, as tool.finished's summary.

after.description: The chat message (history_message id) it came after; null before the first.

hello.description: Sidecar -> Godot, first message after connecting. Followed by one session.snapshot per live session, then sync.completed. Godot refuses a protocol version it doesn't know.

sync.completed.description: Sidecar -> Godot. The initial snapshots after hello are all sent.

ok.description: Sidecar -> Godot, success reply to the command with the same id. The result shape depends on the command (see each command's description).

error.description: Sidecar -> Godot. With id: the command with that id failed. Without id: a protocol-level error (e.g. invalid message).

code.description: Machine-readable: invalid_message (not JSON, not a command, fails the schema, or names no pending permission/question), unknown_provider, unknown_session (none, or it ended), session_starting (created but not up yet), not_supported (capability or extension not declared), invalid_project (path not absolute or not a folder), provider_error (the provider failed; details stay in the sidecar's log).

session.snapshot.description: Sidecar -> Godot. Full state of a session that already exists: after hello, after session.get_snapshot, or when attaching. Godot places the island without the rise animation and replaces whatever it had for this session.

session.created.description: Sidecar -> Godot. A new session started; Godot plays the rise animation.

session.ended.description: Sidecar -> Godot. The session is gone from the registry; Godot sinks its island.

reason.description: user: ended from this app. exited: the session stopped on its own or was closed elsewhere. error: it crashed.

session.notice.description: Sidecar -> Godot. A notice about the session; it replaces an earlier one with the same code. Also listed in the snapshot's notices.

session.updated.description: Sidecar -> Godot. Some of the session's own fields changed; only the changed ones are sent. native_id: the provider started a new conversation in the same session (e.g. Claude Code's /clear), same project. title: the session's name changed (e.g. the provider named it, or the user renamed it); null when it has none yet. mode: the permission mode changed (permission_modes capability).

agent.spawned.description: Sidecar -> Godot. A new agent appeared in the session.

agent.state_changed.description: Sidecar -> Godot. An agent's state changed.

message.started.description: Sidecar -> Godot. A chat message begins. User messages are included, so text typed in the terminal shows up too.

message.delta.description: Sidecar -> Godot. Streamed text to append to the message.

message.completed.description: Sidecar -> Godot. The message is finished; text is the full Markdown and replaces the streamed deltas.

tool.started.description: Sidecar -> Godot. An agent started a tool call (for the C04 log).

within.description: A subagent's call: the tool call that started that subagent (e.g. Claude's Agent call). Absent for the orchestrator's own calls, or when unknown.

tool.finished.description: Sidecar -> Godot. A tool call ended.

permission.requested.description: Sidecar -> Godot. An agent waits on a permission prompt. Its state also changes to waiting with reason "permission".

permission.resolved.description: Sidecar -> Godot. A permission request was answered, here (by: app) or in the terminal (by: external). Godot clears the prompt.

question.asked.description: Sidecar -> Godot (questions capability). An agent asks the user clarifying questions. Its state also changes to waiting with reason "question".

question.resolved.description: Sidecar -> Godot (questions capability). The questions were answered, here (by: app) or in the provider's own interface (by: external); a pending question may show in both. Godot clears them.

plan.asked.description: Sidecar -> Godot (plans capability). An agent asks the user to approve its plan. Its state also changes to waiting with reason "plan". The plan may also show in the provider's own interface; whichever side answers first wins.

plan.resolved.description: Sidecar -> Godot (plans capability). The plan was approved or sent back, here (by: app) or in the provider's own interface (by: external). Godot clears it.

usage.updated.description: Sidecar -> Godot (usage capability). The session's token usage changed; usage holds the whole current figures and replaces the last.

session.create.description: Godot -> sidecar. Start a new session. Reply result: {"session": <id>, "notice"?: notice}; session.created follows. A notice (e.g. confirm_in_terminal) is what to tell the user until then; if the session still isn't up after a minute or two, Godot says it's still starting.

session.list_stored.description: Godot -> sidecar. List resumable sessions the provider has stored (S04). Reply result: {"sessions": [stored_session, ...]}, newest first.

project.description: Only sessions for this project path.

session.resume.description: Godot -> sidecar. Resume a stored session (S04). Reply result: {"session": <id>, "notice"?: notice}, as for session.create; session.created follows.

session.end.description: Godot -> sidecar. End a session (S05). session.ended follows.

interrupt.request.description: Godot -> sidecar (interrupt capability). Stop what the session is doing. The capability's config says whether the stop is immediate or happens at the next step. The session stays open; agent.state_changed events follow.

session.get_snapshot.description: Godot -> sidecar. Resend a session's full state, e.g. after a seq gap. A session.snapshot follows the ok reply.

session.get_history.description: Godot -> sidecar. Fetch the chat history, e.g. when the chat panel opens. Reply result: {"messages": [history_message, ...], "tools": [history_tool, ...]}, each oldest first.

message.send.description: Godot -> sidecar. The user sends a chat message to the orchestrator. message.started (role user) follows.

permission.respond.description: Godot -> sidecar. Answer a permission request (C05). permission.resolved follows.

note.description: Optional message to the agent, e.g. why it was denied.

option.description: Allow only: allow this way, one of the permission's options.

plan.answer.description: Godot -> sidecar (plans capability). Approve a plan, switching to one of its modes, or send it back with an optional note (what to change). plan.resolved follows.

mode.description: With approve: the mode to switch to, one of the plan's modes.

note.description: Without approve: what the agent should change.

question.answer.description: Godot -> sidecar (questions capability). Answer a question set with either answers or a free response. question.resolved follows.

answers.description: One entry per item, in order: the chosen option labels, or the user's own typed text as a single entry.

response.description: A free reply instead of answering the items.

extension.description: Either direction. Provider-specific message, type ext.<provider>.<name>. Only sent for sessions whose extensions list the provider. Session-scoped ones carry session (and seq from the sidecar); commands carry id. Payload schemas live in protocol/ext/<provider>.schema.json.
